knowledge.plain_language_summary: Option 2 of three for the projecting blade sign. A smaller blade than option 1: a painted aluminum body with a laser-cut acrylic decorative applique and article word, and the venue name set as open-faced channel letters lit by exposed amber lamps. No push-thru letters and no faux neon.
knowledge.rationale: Trading push-thru and faux neon for flush-mounted acrylic applique plus open-faced exposed-lamp letters is simpler and cheaper to build than option 1 while keeping the warm exposed-lamp marquee character.
knowledge.tradeoffs: Less luminous depth than option 1 (no glowing push-thru faces), but fewer failure points and a cleaner daytime read from the dimensional applique.
knowledge.when_to_use: When the marquee character is wanted at a lower fabrication cost and smaller footprint than the maximalist option.

rules_observations: Single dominant venue name with a subordinate decorative applique keeps one primary read.
craft_observations: Flush-mounted laser-cut acrylic applique gives daytime dimension; open-faced exposed-lamp letters carry the marquee character at night with the simplest possible lit construction.
Two-tone gold/red palette with a wood-ash pinstripe reads as a restrained version of the marquee idiom.

aesthetic_notes.note: The middle option: marquee character with less hardware than option 1, more dimension than a flat sign.
